answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when misbehavior is proven, so a fake identity carries a real price. A reputation pulse then builds only from verified work over time, like an ember that grows slowly and dies fast when abused. On the tundra of anonymous accounts this stake-and-history bond makes a Sybil swarm expensive: an attacker must fund every fake, and one bad act burns its stake, so honest agents stay cheap while fakes pay dearly.
